exposure: Maternal country of birth (Eastern African: Eritrea, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan vs. Australian-born)
cohort: The study included 237,943 Australian-born women and 4,057 Eastern African immigrant women giving singleton birth in public care in Victoria, Australia.
finding: Primiparae and multiparae born in Eastern African countries had significantly elevated odds of first-time unplanned caesarean in labour, and generally higher odds of any first-time caesarean, compared to Australian-born women.
mod_finding: The study observed substantial variations in first-time caesarean section rates, both unplanned in labour and overall, between Eastern African immigrant women and Australian-born women, which were not explained by socio-demographic and clinical risks.
